# `pi_station_list`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the saved Wi-Fi networks of the device.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds); it is a mutator because the packaged script can run a reconfigure step. |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe3d10, ns_net::pi_station_list @0x700760 (64-bit build) |

Runs the packaged network script to list the networks saved in the device's Wi-Fi configuration (not scan results) and returns their names. Despite being a list, on models other than the Plus and Mini the call first makes the supplicant reload its configuration (see side effects), so it is not observation-safe on all models. The 32-bit network script lacks the detailed listing action, so only plain names are expected there (INFERRED).

Side effects: Synchronously runs a shell script (list_config, falling back to list). The device passes 1 on Plus and Mini models and 0 otherwise; the packaged scripts call a Wi-Fi supplicant reconfigure before listing unless the argument is 1, so other models have their network configuration reloaded, which can briefly disturb an active station link; this is not a guaranteed disconnection. ret_obj changes only the reply wrapping. The process read can block with no established deadline.

## Example

Request, default - Typical request (the app sends no params):

```json
{"id":81,"method":"pi_station_list"}
```

Request, wrapped - Object-wrapped reply:

```json
{"id":82,"method":"pi_station_list","params":{"ret_obj":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_list","result":["Example network",{"ssid":"Hidden example","hidden":true}],"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, ok-wrapped-empty:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_list","result":{"value":[]},"code":0,"id":82}
```

Reply, no-output:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_list","error":"no result from command","code":223,"id":83}
```
